title: Slow-Cooker Chilli Con Carne
subtitle: Hearty beef and kidney bean chilli cooked low and slow
excerpt: Beef mince browned with onions, garlic, and spices, then cooked low and slow with tinned tomatoes and kidney beans until the sauce is thick and deeply flavoured. Better the next day. Serve with rice and soured cream.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chilli con carne originated in Texas in the 19th century and entered British home cooking through American influence in the 1970s and 1980s. The slow cooker version benefits greatly from the low-and-slow method: the spices have time to bloom, the beef becomes more tender, and the tomato sauce thickens into something richer than the 30-minute stovetop version. Browning the mince first is essential for flavour.

content.text: Brown the mince well before it goes into the slow cooker: a pale, steamed mince has little flavour. Break the mince up as you cook it and let it take on some colour. The kidney beans go in for the final hour only: added at the start they become too soft. Season at the end when the flavour has concentrated.

Brown the beef mince in a large frying pan over high heat in two batches, breaking it up with a wooden spoon. Transfer to the slow cooker. In the same pan, cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, chilli powder, cumin, smoked paprika, coriander, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for another minute. Transfer to the slow cooker.
Add the tinned tomatoes, beef stock, and Worcestershire sauce to the slow cooker. Stir to combine. Cook on LOW for 5 to 6 hours or HIGH for 3 to 4 hours.
Add the drained kidney beans and the dark chocolate in the final hour of cooking. Stir in, replace the lid, and continue cooking.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with rice, soured cream, and grated Cheddar.
